newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile to put Central Bank nominee up for new vote.
newsitem.headline: Chile to put Central Bank nominee up for new vote.

text.p: The Chilean government will offer economist Carlos Massad's nomination to the Central Bank board for another vote in the Senate after it was narrowly rejected Tuesday, Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat said.
Aninat, speaking after a clear majority of senators asked President Eduardo Frei to resubmit the nomination, said he expected lawmakers to vote again on Massad by next Tuesday.
"We are now preparing the papers to place Massad's candidacy before the Senate again," Aninat told reporters.

Aninat was speaking after 25 senators -- an absolute majority in the 47-member body -- sent Frei a letter asking him to resubmit the nomination, saying the 21-20 vote against Massad did not represent the chamber's true feeling.
If approved, Massad would join the bank's five-member board to replace Roberto Zahler, the bank president who quit in June. The board will then elect a president.
